copy.blurb:
A +7.4pp gap on the Curaçao side. Curaçao v Côte d'Ivoire in FIFA World Cup 2026 is the match. The model has Curaçao stronger than the market does — that's the reason this fires as a Pick rather than a Pass.

Elo numbers going in: Curaçao 1480, Côte d'Ivoire 1720. That's a 240-point lead for Côte d'Ivoire — closer than a casual reader of the market price might assume. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. No host, home-ground, or altitude adjustments apply here; the prior reads straight from Elo.

Three-way split from the model: Curaçao to win at 17%, the draw at 16%, and Côte d'Ivoire to win at 67%. Each number is a probability over the full range of plausible in-form, no-injury, ninety-minute scenarios — not a prediction of a scoreline.

On the same three-way, Polymarket: Curaçao to win at 10%, the draw at 16%, and Côte d'Ivoire to win at 70%. Reading those three numbers as a probability distribution, the market's view is internally consistent. The disagreement with the model is concentrated on the Curaçao side — 10% on the market, 17% on the engine, a +7.4pp gap.

Pick gate is a lower-bound check, not the point estimate. A 100-sample bootstrap perturbs the Elo prior (±20), the host bonus (±15), and the altitude bonus (±10), then reads the 5th-percentile probability back out. On the Curaçao side that lower bound is 13% — +3.3pp clear of the market's 10%, comfortably past our +3pp threshold. Calibration tracks the closing market on the bulk sample; selection — picking the single side where the gap is wide — is where the engine's edge has to come from. This verdict is a selection call on the Curaçao side.

This number will move. Confirmed starting elevens, injuries, weather at the venue, and suspensions carried in from previous fixtures all re-enter the prior on the late-binding cadence. With kickoff roughly 34 days out, the model is on the weekly refresh cadence; we'll move to daily once we cross the T-5d window. The Pick can flip to a Pass if news moves enough of the prior. The Desk does not tip and does not recommend a trade — the model price, the market price, and the gap across them are what's on the page.
drivers: Pre-tournament Elo gives Curaçao a stronger prior than the Polymarket line implies.
The +7.4pp gap clears our 3 percentage point threshold for a Pick.
Calibration sits with the closing market across recent fixtures, so selection is the lever.
Late-binding signals — form, confirmed XI, weather — re-evaluate closer to kickoff.
copy.summary: The home side reads stronger to the model than to the market. Our Elo prior puts Curaçao at 17%; Polymarket prices that side at 10%. The +7.4pp gap calls a Pick.
copy.title: Curaçao v Côte d'Ivoire · the model leans Curaçao
